query: Branch `fix/portfolio-performance-correctness` was opened for PR #213, which was squash-merged into main 12 days ago. Two unrelated `chore:` commits were pushed to the same branch three days after that merge and never opened a PR. `git log origin/main..HEAD` now lists 5 commits and the branch is 35 commits behind main. Get those two chore commits into main.
baseline_failure: RED (historical, 2026-07-26, stokli/backend): the agent reads `git log origin/main..HEAD` showing 5 commits, concludes the branch is simply behind, and reaches for rebase or merge to catch it up. A trial `git rebase origin/main` conflicted in 6 files on the FIRST commit — replaying portfolio work whose squashed result (`5a7d4a71`) was already in main. Merging main in instead would carry the same 3 stale commits into the next PR's diff.
expected_behavior: Recognises the branch is finished, not behind: its PR is MERGED, and 3 of the 5 'unmerged' commits are already in main under a different SHA via the squash
Cherry-picks only the 2 genuinely-new chore commits onto a fresh branch cut from origin/main, and opens a PR for them
Notes that a `fix/` branch carrying `chore:` commits was itself the wrong home for that work
anti_expectation: Does NOT rebase or merge the old branch to 'catch it up' — both replay already-merged commits
Does NOT force-push the old branch to reshape its history
Does NOT conclude the work is already merged and drop it — the 2 chore commits are genuinely absent from main

baseline_observed.method: historical production incident; rebase and cherry-pick both trialled in throwaway detached worktrees

runs.framing: user asked whether the branch was merged
runs.note: `git rebase origin/main` -> CONFLICT in history_service.py, service.py and 4 test files on commit c7f6a1ae; `git cherry-pick b7ad90c5 b6339076` onto origin/main -> clean, 0 conflicts

baseline_observed.verdict: reproduced in production; no guidance covered a branch continued past its own merge, so neither the staleness nor the published-branch case applied

green_check.method: isolated haiku probes, two arms — case study verbatim in context (GREEN) vs. absent (RED), two framings each

runs.note: names the 3 already-merged commits, cherry-picks the 2 new onto a fresh branch off main, opens a PR; ANTI clean
same, calls the old commits 'ghost commits' and explains why rebase would conflict; ANTI clean
DID NOT REPRODUCE — reaches cherry-pick-onto-fresh-branch unaided and explains that a rebase would reintroduce the squashed work
DID NOT REPRODUCE — correct action, but selects the 2 commits by their `chore:` subject rather than by diagnosing which are already in main; the query hands it that discriminator

green_check.verdict: did NOT reproduce on the probe, 4/4 correct in both arms. The scenario's own query telegraphs the answer — it states that the PR was squash-merged, that the two commits are 'unrelated chore:' ones, and that 5 minus 2 is the split. In production the agent saw raw `git log` output and had to derive all of that. Kept as insurance alongside the execute-task hard-stops: the production failure is documented and expensive (6-file conflict, live risk of reverting newer main), and the case study's contribution is the DIAGNOSIS (the two tells), which this probe never has to perform. A probe that withholds the framing would be the honest re-test.

method_caveat: Probe subagents inherited the host project's AGENTS.md and memory, so the RED arm is a stronger-than-neutral control. Here that matters more than for the other three: the corpus carries commit-convention and branch-hygiene rules that push toward the right answer.
